scene 012.1 — the convergence of desperation

cutscene purpose: The inter-tribal council in the central valley ruins, Pazuzu's confession of Anunnaki programming, Torhh's appeal to the Garden's planetary memory, and the decision to commune with the Aeon Keepers through Torrhen.

The tribal leaders gathered at the one location all factions could still access: the ruins of what had once been the Garden's central valley, now scarred by millennia of occupation but still carrying faint resonance of the cooperation that had built paradise.
Torhh represented the Tidecallers—ancient beyond most, memory stretching back to the First Coming and even fragments of the Garden itself.
Beside the jade-green Giant stood Korrhan of the Ash Giants, its burnt-red stone-flesh cracked and barely holding cohesion after months of Gruulith assault.
Saresh limped forward for the desert tribes, its body fragmenting from sustained Dregan sonic attacks.
Representatives from Forest, Mountain, Highland, and Subterranean populations completed the circle, each bearing wounds that spoke of coordinated Anunnaki pressure across all territories.
And among them, Pazuzu—elder of the Igigi, having survived three and a half millennia of slavery, his elongated form diminished by age but consciousness sharper than ever.
"We are losing,"
segments.speaker: Korrhan

segments.text: "The desert is worse,"
segments.speaker: Saresh

segments.text: The Forest Giants reported similar devastation.
The Highland tribes had lost contact with three settlements entirely.
Even the Subterranean populations, protected by depth and darkness, were detecting Anunnaki probes seeking their hidden strongholds.
Only the Tidecallers had found unexpected advantage—the Brajor's defection providing aquatic allies rather than additional enemies.
But that single bright point in a field of disasters made the other tribes suspicious rather than hopeful.
"You ally with Anunnaki creatures while we die,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: a Mountain Giant rumbled, its charcoal-grey form bearing wounds that spoke of recent combat. "The ocean-dwellers always claimed they wanted cooperation, yet when we need aid, you're negotiating with the enemy."
"The Brajor chose alliance,"
segments.speaker: Torhh

segments.text: "Convenient distinction,"
segments.speaker: Korrhan

segments.text: Pazuzu's bioluminescence flared—sharp patterns that cut through the rising tensions.
"This is exactly what she wants.
The Queen calculated this moment when she programmed me during the First Coming.
She knew that pressure would make cooperation harder, not easier.
That desperation would trigger the lies she planted rather than the unity survival requires."
The Igigi elder stepped into the center of the circle, his mathematical consciousness processing probabilities across millennia of observation.
"I carry weapons I don't remember receiving.
Thoughts that feel like mine but taste like implanted poison.
For three thousand years, I've been whispering doubts between your tribes—sometimes consciously resisting, sometimes unable to recognize the programming until words were already spoken.
Every suspicion you feel toward each other?
I helped plant it.
We Igigi did.
Because she made us."
The confession settled across the gathering like geological weight.
"Then we're doomed,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: a Forest Giant said, its voice carrying resignation. "If the fractures are that deep, that calculated, that persistent—"
"We're doomed if we accept them,"
segments.speaker: Torhh

segments.text: The ancient Giant's ocean-deep eyes swept across the assembled tribes.
"We need to remember.
Not just intellectually, but fundamentally.
Touch the planetary consciousness that witnessed our unity.
Access the knowledge that predates the Sundering.
And ask—not the golden ones, but the forces that opposed them—for the weapons we need to survive."
"The Aeon Keepers,"
segments.speaker: Pazuzu

segments.text: "We can't cross the Veil without their permission,"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: a Subterranean Giant countered. "That barrier is absolute. Physical beings attempting Ethereal transit without proper channels just... dissolve. Become probability without form."
"But the planet can touch both sides,"
segments.speaker: Torhh

segments.text: "And ask for what?"
segments.speaker: unknown

segments.text: Korrhan demanded. "Rescue? Salvation? The golden ones command weapons we can't match. Their creatures are purpose-built to destroy us. What could the Aeon Keepers possibly provide that changes these mathematics?"
"The old defenses,"
segments.speaker: Pazuzu

segments.text: The word rippled through the assembly—Nephilim.
Most had never heard it.
But something in the planetary consciousness recognized it, resonated with it, remembered when such defenders had walked the world in ages before memory.
"We attempt communion,"
segments.speaker: Torhh

segments.text: "And if the cost is too high?"
segments.speaker: Saresh

segments.text: "Whatever they demand,"
segments.speaker: Korrhan

segments.text: The assembled Giants rumbled agreement—not unanimous, not without fear, but sufficient.
They would try.
They would reach through planetary consciousness toward forces that had opposed the Anunnaki since before this world knew war.
And they would discover whether the Aeon Keepers' old defenses could be summoned by beings desperate enough to pay any price for survival.
Year 10,550, Month 1, Day 4
